root_cause.text: In the Bluetooth MGMT subsystem's `tlv_data_is_valid()` function, the parser accesses the type byte at `data[i + 1]` before validating that the current field's length does not exceed the remaining buffer size, allowing an out-of-bounds read on malformed input.
root_cause.evidence: The patch reorders the code in `net/bluetooth/mgmt.c` to move the buffer boundary check `if (i + cur_len >= len)` prior to the type checks `if (data[i + 1] == ...)`, directly addressing the KASAN-reported out-of-bounds read in `tlv_data_is_valid()`.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement accesses data[i + 1] to read the type byte without first validating that i + 1 is within the valid buffer range. The preceding check at line 8644 validates 'i + cur_len >= len' but this may not properly protect against out-of-bounds access when cur_len is small or zero, allowing malformed input to trigger an out-of-bounds read on the data array.
